I will still do what I did in the last few years: keep most land in wheat-maize and leave only a small piece for cotton. We are only 2 people at home, and some work is off-farm, so I will not put too much land into cotton because cotton needs more watching and more spraying. Around here, if wheat and maize get enough fertilizer and water from the well, the harvest is steadier and the money is more certain. I learned from my own field and from the neighbors who get good yields: wheat cannot be short of bottom fertilizer, maize cannot be short of nitrogen after the wheat stubble, and cotton needs more potash and more pesticide trips or the bolls do not hold well. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield. So this year I will put 18 mu into the wheat-maize rotation and 6 mu into cotton. For wheat, I will use improved seed, give a full base dressing, water about 3 times if the season is normal, and aim for about 550 kg per mu. After wheat harvest, I will no-till or lightly open the rows and plant hybrid maize on the same 18 mu, push nitrogen a bit harder, water 2 times with the well, and aim for 600 kg per mu. Cotton I will keep on 6 mu only, use improved seed, not save on potash, irrigate 3 times, spray more often than grain crops, and aim for about 320 kg per mu of seed cotton.
